intended_object: The canonical inclusion into B of the "value group with zero" of f : A →*₀ B: 0 adjoined to the subgroup of Bˣ generated by the invertible values of f, mapped into B by 0 ↦ 0 and each unit u ↦ u. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body extends the subgroup inclusion valueGroup f → Bˣ to WithZero (valueGroup f) → WithZero Bˣ with WithZero.map', then applies WithZero.withZeroUnitsEquiv : WithZero Bˣ ≃* B. This is exactly the map described: 0 ↦ 0 and each unit u ↦ u. It is a monoid-with-zero hom, and the next lemma in the file (embedding_injective) shows it is injective, matching the word "embedding". A only needs to be a MonoidWithZero, which is fully general. B is assumed to be a GroupWithZero. The bare map WithZero Bˣ →*₀ B would make sense for any monoid with zero B, but WithZero.withZeroUnitsEquiv is only an equivalence when B is a group with zero. The docstring's reading of the image as "the subgroup with zero generated by the range of f" also only holds then: in a general monoid with zero, nonzero non-units in the range of f would be missing from the image. The companion definition restrict₀ likewise needs every nonzero value of f to be a unit. So the group-with-zero setting is the natural one for this construction, and widening it would be at most a minor tweak. I know of no separate Mathlib declaration of the same embedding; it is just the composite of the general constructions WithZero.map' and WithZero.withZeroUnitsEquiv.
